message.reasoning_content:
The kernel: symmetric sigmoid trick, exp(-|x|), where(x<0, exp/(1+exp), 1/(1+exp)). This is exact in FP32 for most cases? exp in fp32 has ~1ulp error; then division rn. The question: does final FP16 rounding always match correctly-rounded sigmoid? FP32 has enough precision generally (fp32 relative error ~2^-24, fp16 step ~2^-11), so intermediate fp32 rounding can't flip the fp16 result unless the exact value is within 2^-24 of a fp16 tie point. exp itself has error, so near tie boundaries could flip. Worth testing exhaustively over all finite FP16 inputs (65536 values, minus nonfinite ≈ 65504 values). That's feasible.

Claim: kernel output matches reference bit-exactly for all finite FP16 inputs. Test exhaustively.
